Business Model: Tokenized Treasury products; earns through product fees, spread, and distribution of on-chain yield products
Underlying Assets: OUSG: tokenized exposure to U.S. Treasuries and institutional money market funds; USDY: tokenized note backed by short-term U.S. Treasuries and bank deposits
Investor Access: OUSG: qualified purchasers / institutional investors; USDY: qualifying non-U.S. investors
Token Standard / Transfer Restrictions: Transfer restrictions and eligibility controls; USDY has accumulating and rebasing versions
Custody / Administrator: Ondo entities plus disclosed fund/custody partners depending on product
Redemption Mechanics: OUSG supports instant USDC redemption when liquidity is available and standard next-business-day processing; USDY redemption subject to product rules
Yield Source: Treasury / money market fund yield after fees
Key Strength: Strong bridge between DeFi distribution and familiar Treasury exposure
Key Weakness: Product structure differs by token; legal claim and redemption terms require close reading

Business Model: Tokenized institutional liquidity fund distributed and administered through Securitize
Underlying Assets: Cash, U.S. Treasury bills, and repurchase agreements
Investor Access: Qualified institutional investors / eligible investors through Securitize
Primary Chain(s): Ethereum and additional supported chains through Securitize ecosystem
Token Standard / Transfer Restrictions: Permissioned tokenized fund shares with transfer controls
Custody / Administrator: BlackRock fund; Securitize as tokenization / transfer agent platform; named service providers in fund docs
Redemption Mechanics: Subscription and redemption through Securitize / fund process
Yield Source: Short-duration Treasury and cash management yield
Compliance / KYC: KYC / AML and investor eligibility through Securitize
Key Strength: Highest institutional brand signal and strong market validation
Key Weakness: Access is institution-focused; token utility depends on permissioned ecosystem liquidity

Business Model: U.S.-registered money market fund with blockchain-integrated recordkeeping and distribution through Benji
Underlying Assets: U.S. government securities, cash, and repurchase agreements held by Franklin OnChain U.S. Government Money Fund
Investor Access: Investors onboarded through Franklin / Benji channels; availability depends on jurisdiction and eligibility
Primary Chain(s): Stellar plus additional supported public blockchains
Token Standard / Transfer Restrictions: Fund share recordkeeping on public blockchain; transferability subject to fund and platform rules
Custody / Administrator: Franklin Templeton transfer agency and fund infrastructure
Redemption Mechanics: Redeemable through fund / Benji process; settlement and transfer features depend on supported rails
Yield Source: Money market fund income from government securities and repo
Compliance / KYC: KYC / AML and fund investor requirements
Key Strength: Most directly resembles a regulated mutual fund, making TradFi comparison clean
Key Weakness: Less crypto-native composability; product is still bounded by fund rules and investor eligibility

Business Model: On-chain credit marketplace and asset management platform; earns management/service fees from lending products
Underlying Assets: Cash management pool: Treasury bills and reverse repos through borrower SPV; broader Maple pools include secured institutional loans
Investor Access: Accredited or eligible institutional lenders depending on pool; AML checks and minimum deposit for cash management
Token Standard / Transfer Restrictions: ERC-4626 style LP tokens in permissioned pools; transfers subject to allowlist controls
Custody / Administrator: Pool delegate / borrower SPV such as Room40 for cash management; external custody and counterparties by pool
Redemption Mechanics: Withdrawals subject to pool liquidity and stated processing windows
Yield Source: SOFR-linked Treasury/repo yield for cash management; credit spread for lending pools
Fees: Cash management docs cite 50 bps annualized fees
Key Strength: Shows how RWA can move beyond Treasuries into institutional credit
Key Weakness: Credit and counterparty risk are more important than in pure Treasury products

Product(s): Tokenized private credit / structured credit pools
Business Model: Tokenization and fund infrastructure for issuers and investors; platform supports asset managers launching compliant tokenized funds
Underlying Assets: Private credit, structured credit, receivables, real-world collateral, and fund interests depending on issuer
Investor Access: Whitelisted / eligible investors; permissions depend on pool and jurisdiction
Primary Chain(s): Centrifuge protocol with multi-chain integrations including Ethereum/EVM environments
Token Standard / Transfer Restrictions: Permissioned investment and redemption flows; pool tokens / tranche-like structures depending on product
Custody / Administrator: Issuer, asset manager, and pool service providers define custody and administration
Redemption Mechanics: Investors submit investment and redemption orders subject to pool rules and available liquidity
Yield Source: Asset cash flows from private credit / structured finance assets
Compliance / KYC: KYC / investor whitelisting and compliance controls
Key Strength: Closest to ABS-style thinking: asset pools, tranching, issuer workflow, waterfalls
Key Weakness: Harder to diligence because asset quality varies materially by pool and issuer
